The prime of interest is \(p = 503\) and the modulus for the binomial sums is \(502 = p-1\). Write \(10000\) in base \(p\):

\[
10000 = 19 \cdot 503 + 443, \qquad 0 \le 443 < 503.
\]

For any \(k\) with \(0 \le k \le 10000\), write \(k = 503a + b\) where \(0 \le a \le 19\) and \(0 \le b \le 502\). By Lucas' theorem,

\[
\binom{10000}{k} \equiv \binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b} \pmod{503}.
\]

Note that \(\binom{443}{b}=0\) for \(b > 443\).

The condition defining \(S_r\) is \(k \equiv r \pmod{502}\). Since \(503 \equiv 1 \pmod{502}\),

\[
k = 503a + b \equiv a + b \pmod{502}.
\]

Thus

\[
S_r \equiv \sum_{a=0}^{19}\sum_{b=0}^{502} [a+b \equiv r \pmod{502}] \binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b} \pmod{503}.
\]

Because \(\binom{443}{b}=0\) for \(b>443\), we may restrict \(b\) to \(0 \le b \le 443\). For these \(a,b\) we have

\[
a + b \le 19 + 443 = 462 < 502.
\]

Hence \(a+b\) lies in \([0,462]\). The congruence \(a+b \equiv r \pmod{502}\) can only be satisfied if

- \(a+b = r\) when \(0 \le r \le 462\) (since \(r+502 > 462\)), or
- there is no solution when \(463 \le r \le 501\) (because \(r-502 < 0\) and \(r > 462\)).

Therefore

\[
S_r \equiv 
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{a+b=r} \binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b} = \binom{462}{r} \pmod{503}, & 0 \le r \le 462,\\[0.5em]
0 \pmod{503}, & 463 \le r \le 501.
\end{cases}
\]

Since \(462 < 503\), the prime \(503\) does not divide any \(\binom{462}{r}\) for \(0 \le r \le 462\) (the numerator \(462!\) contains no factor \(503\)). Hence \(\binom{462}{r} \not\equiv 0 \pmod{503}\) for these \(r\).

Consequently, \(S_r\) is a multiple of \(503\) precisely when \(463 \le r \le 501\). The number of such \(r\) is

\[
501 - 463 + 1 = 39.
\]

The list includes \(S_0\) through \(S_{501}\); \(S_0\) is not a multiple, so the total count is \(39\).

\[
\boxed{39}
\]
